classification.difficultyReason: Translate the claim into a condition on the derivative, then use the product and chain rules and establish positivity for every real x.

content.prompt: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Show that the curve $$f(x)=x(x^2+1)^n$$ has no horizontal tangents.

answer.short:
There are no horizontal tangents.

The product rule gives $f'(x)=(x^2+1)^{n-1}[(2n+1)x^2+1]>0$ for all real $x$.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}f'(x)&=(x^2+1)^n+2nx^2(x^2+1)^{n-1}\\f'(x)&=(x^2+1)^{n-1}[(x^2+1)+2nx^2]\\f'(x)&=(x^2+1)^{n-1}[(2n+1)x^2+1]\end{align*}$$ Both factors are positive for every real $x$, since $x^2\ge 0$ and $n\ge 1$. Thus $f'(x)>0$ everywhere, so the curve has no horizontal tangents.
